# Glue

Manage the Data Catalog, classify and crawl S3 data, and orchestrate local Python shell ETL jobs and workflows.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `glue` |
| Signing name | `glue` |
| Wire protocol | AWS JSON 1.1 |
| API version | `2017-03-31` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Records / local S3 crawling / optional local Python host execution |
| Selected operations | 70 of 306 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#glue) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- Spark (glueetl/gluestreaming) and Ray (glueray) definitions are stored, but StartJobRun explicitly rejects execution because TinyStack has no Spark/Ray runtime.
- EVENT triggers, connections, Glue Studio and managed production engines are not implemented; unsupported members fail explicitly.
- Python scripts use the configured host python3 and its installed packages, not a managed Glue Python distribution; the awsglue library is unavailable and scripts must not import it.
- Python shell execution is enabled only when the selected Lambda executor is local; otherwise runs fail with: Local execution is disabled: select the Lambda local executor (lambda.executor: local) to run Glue Python shell jobs.
- Scripts execute with the TinyStack user privileges; this shares Lambda local execution settings and process-group lifecycle, not a sandbox.
- Bookmarks are not emulated: GetJobBookmark and ResetJobBookmark are unsupported rather than returning invented progress.
- A claimed RUNNING process is killed on shutdown; its durable run becomes FAILED with an explicit interrupted-execution error after restart, never silently SUCCEEDED; queued STARTING runs resume.
- Cron L/W/# extensions are explicitly unsupported by the shared parser; missed schedule times are skipped rather than replayed.
- StartWorkflowRun selects exactly one ON_DEMAND source trigger; scheduled or directly started source triggers also create workflow runs; trigger renaming is unsupported.
- Grok/XML classifiers and JDBC, MongoDB, DynamoDB, Catalog, Delta, Iceberg and Hudi crawler targets fail explicitly; Catalog and DynamoDB discovery are not implemented. S3 target connections and event-queue (S3 event mode) crawls fail explicitly when set.
- Crawler Configuration accepts only Version 1.0; grouping overrides including CombineCompatibleSchemas and other configuration keys fail explicitly.
- Custom JSONPath supports $, $[*] and dotted member paths with optional final [*]; other expressions fail explicitly. Athena retains its JSON-lines reader and does not interpret custom JSONPath.
- CSV custom datatype overrides support bigint, double, boolean, string and timestamp; other types fail explicitly. Athena supports double-quoted CSV only.
- Crawler grouping merges identical compatible schemas under a target folder; incompatible schemas sharing one root fail rather than inventing a table location. AWS proprietary probabilistic grouping and header heuristics are approximated.
- Crawler exclusions support *, **, ?, and character classes; brace alternation fails explicitly. ListCrawls supports STATE EQ filters only. Estimated remaining time is unavailable (zero with StillEstimating while running).
- A claimed crawl interrupted by shutdown becomes FAILED on restart with an explicit interruption message; an unclaimed RUNNING crawl resumes, and STOPPING completes CANCELLED. Crawl catalog writes commit atomically after S3 reads, so stopped crawls publish no tables.
- Crawl output messages use /aws-glue/crawlers with the crawler name as stream; crawling is available independently of the Python executor.
- Job logs become visible after each attempt finishes; ErrorMessage retains at most the last 8192 bytes of stderr.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.

JSON/Query endpoint. RPC v2 CBOR uses its service/operation route, as described in
[protocol handling](../architecture/request-flow.md). Supported members are selected separately in the
